trial_court: V Addl. Judge, Family Court, Bangalore, MC No.1043/2012
case_name: S Kumara Swamy vs Smt P Mala
facts_of_case: Appellant and respondent got married in 2005. Respondent's mother interfered with their marital life. Appellant requested respondent to join the matrimonial home, but she refused. She filed a police complaint against appellant and his family members for alleged offences under IPC. The criminal case is pending.

legal_principles.principle: Mere filing of a police complaint does not amount to mental cruelty unless the jurisdictional court gives a finding that the initiation of the case is malicious and false.
legal_principles.held: In the absence of any such finding, we are of the opinion that mere filing of a police complaint ipso facto does not amount to mental cruelty.
cited_cases: RANI NARASIMHA SASTRY Vs. RANI SUNEELA RANI, (2020) 18 SCC 247

legal_principles.principle: When a person undergoes a trial in which he is acquitted of the allegation of offence under Section 498-A of IPC, it cannot be accepted that no cruelty has meted on the husband.
legal_principles.held: But when a person undergoes a trial in which he is acquitted of the allegation of offence under Section 498-A of IPC, levelled by the wife against the husband, it cannot be accepted that no cruelty has meted on the husband.
cited_cases: RAJ TALREJA Vs. KAVITA TALREJA, [(2017) 14 SCC 194]

outcome.final_order: The petition seeking dissolution of marriage was dismissed by the trial court, and this dismissal is upheld on appeal.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
seeking relief from Indian Penal Code
